images.caption: Figure 1:RoTA-Bench overview. The benchmark contains 674 canonical tasks, with 100 test tasks selected by stratified sampling over reference path lengths. In the T-shirt example, the solver chooses discrete rotations from visual observations and receives updated views until projection IoU reaches0.900.90or another stopping rule applies. The right panel shows task success rates and final IoU on the test set; full results are reported in Table1.

Figure 2:RoTA-Bench construction and evaluation pipeline.(a)(1)Source 2D icons are(2)filtered, sampled, and normalized, then(3)converted into 3D objects through sphere-bounded extrusion.(4)Reversible initialization generates an initial pose with a feasible solution.(5)Pose-guided beam search and30∘30^{\circ}-restricted breadth-first search provide verified reference paths, which are used to select 100 test tasks from 674 canonical tasks by stratified sampling over reference path lengths.(6)The action space contains 24 discrete rotations across three axes, two directions, and four angles.(b)In closed-loop evaluation, the solver selects rotations from visual observations and interaction history, then receives updated observations. Success requires projection IoU≥0.90\geq 0.90.

Figure 6:Human evaluation interface with the same prompt content, current observation, historical observations, and discrete action space used by the models. Humans submit actions through buttons that map to the model action tokens and angles.
